comments.author: ehaugw
comments.body_html:
Technically, this mod doesn’t change anything. It just adds additional behavior. Thus, it is compatible with everything. If it doesn’t work with Realism, it’s Realism not being compatible with this mod.

That being said, it does excessive null checking and will fail gracefully if installed together with incompatible mods

comments.body_html: I haven’t noticed any issues with Fika from this alone, and I don’t use it on the headless client. Which I think makes sense: the headless client is mainly just responsible for AI decisions, and I don’t expect this mod to affect any of that (unless AI PMCs have different skill/mastery levels… maybe). Just my two cents.

comments.author: Prometheus
comments.body_html: Interesting - 15% MOA feels like a lot per level, but maybe I’m crazy. Did you choose this after testing because 5% felt too small, maybe?

comments.author: hellchickens
comments.body_html: Mmmm, the main problem here is that there are mods that elaborate the “stats” on bots and also there is not only bot logic, but there is whole map and player state sync with headless, so different “values” for same things may lead (and leads in most cases) for desyncs and incorrect calculations. Mostly it’s valid for server + client mods, though I’ve already faced few times headless problems with only client mods that have no sync, even if it installed both on actual playing client and headless. So my intention here is to validate if there are any known (or possible by design) issues with headless client or not

comments.author: Prometheus
comments.body_html: Fair enough. For what it’s worth, my group has had stable / normal experiences w/ headless Fika; we run ~53 server mods, ~71 client mods, and ~17 headless mods. There are a couple exceptions (e.g. WTT Pack ‘n Strap), but pretty much the only mods on the headless client are AI mods and mods that explicitly include headless support (UI Fixes, Battle Ambiance, etc). No reported desyncs, even with a couple larger overhaul mods (but we don’t run Realism, FWIW).
